text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in captured req/resp for /v1/classify yesterday that tripped the per-tenant capture budget and evicted sticky captures. :warning:
kevin: ugh. which tenants? any PII exposure?
sam: quick summary: ~1.2k samples over 3h, affinity TTLs expired, new requests fell back to generic sampling so we lost continuity for some debugging flows.
maria: tenant A mostly. no clear PII leak in the stored probes but attachments were captured in a few samples.
olivia: can we avoid eviction wiping affinity immediately? maybe use soft-eviction + LRU grace window so one-off spikes don't scatter traces.
kevin: idea: affinity_key = sha256(tenant_id + route) and keep a small reserved pool (10% of budget) for sticky keys. TTL 24h default, but adjustable per-route.
sam: agreed. also need a policy for PII fields when we keep sticky captures — we should reduce stored payload to fingerprint-only for anything flagged by scrubber.
maria: thumbs up to fingerprint-only for name/email/credit-card. But attachments are tricky — large and often contain PII. proposal: never persist raw attachments, only store metadata + s3 pointer that is access-controlled and auto-deletes after 7d.
olivia: console UX: show a "capture affinity" column in the Debugging dashboard (sticky keys, TTL, reserved budget). Help ops understand why a route might hold capacity.
kevin: for sampling fallback when quota exhausted: return header X-Capture-Status: limited; include token explaining reason (evicted|quota|policy). That helps downstream to instrument.
sam: +1, machine-readable reason is crucial for automations. Also add a short text string for humans in console.
maria: security check — if we persist hashed PII fields, ensure hashes are salted per-tenant and rotated on key rotation. No raw PII in logs.
kevin: capture-bot: scan completed for the thread resources referenced — no raw PII found in the current sample store. :eyes:
capture-bot: scan-id=scan-1797772468 status=ok matches=0
maria: action items: (1) sam draft sampler change (affinity + reserved pool + fallback header) (2) kevin draft redaction rules for sticky captures (hashing + attachment policy) (3) olivia mock console surface and wording. target: quick RFC by EOD Friday.
kevin: i'll start the redaction rules doc.
sam: I'll open the PR for sampler changes and include benchmarks for latency/throughput.
olivia: I'll wireframe the dashboard tile and example header exposure.
maria: cool. if anyone hits edgecases where affinity keeps hogging budget, we can add a low-priority preempt rule.
kevin: noted — prefer preempt over hard-delete to avoid losing debug context.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
